name: Idiopathic Syringomyelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Syringomyelia

criteria.description: Presence of progressive sensory disturbances such as dissociated sensory loss (pain and temperature) in a cape-like distribution
MRI evidence of a syrinx (fluid-filled cavity) within the spinal cord without associated Chiari malformation or other causative lesions
Exclusion of secondary causes such as trauma, tumors, infection, or congenital malformations
Neurological examination showing segmental muscle weakness and atrophy consistent with spinal cord involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical symptoms plus MRI confirmation of syrinx without secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary syringomyelia causes and correlation of clinical and imaging findings.

laboratory: Routine labs typically normal; used to exclude infection or inflammatory causes
imaging: MRI of the spinal cord showing syrinx cavity without associated Chiari malformation or tumor
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated with idiopathic syringomyelia
other: Neurophysiological studies may show segmental denervation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cerebellar tonsillar herniation on MRI
Progressive neurological deficits with localized spinal pain
Syrinx formation at or near site of spinal injury

redFlags: Signs of spinal cord compression or myelopathy
New onset bladder or bowel dysfunction
